To change the server URL for existing config entries, we don't need to use `async_migrate_entry`. We can just check what URL the config entry has stored when setting up the config entry, and update the config entry data if needed before continuing.

We try to avoid migrations that update the config entry version when possible as those make it impossible to roll back for users.

We can update the existing config entry data by passing `updates` parameter here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/65f86ce44fa663c64cbd6f16331fc6e1e9806506/homeassistant/components/growatt_server/config_flow.py#L85

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/65f86ce44fa663c64cbd6f16331fc6e1e9806506/homeassistant/config_entries.py#L1295-L1303

Then the user can just set up a config entry again with the same credentials but a different server URL.

If the option really needs changing more often we can implement an options flow, but server URL doesn't seem to fit that criteria.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/config_entries_options_flow_handler

Honestly, we should just migrate for existing users OR trigger a re-auth to they can adjust. Having this is an option flows makes not much sense so me personally (as a matter of fact, that a user has to choose between a "server" makes no sense from a end-user perspective at all).

Settings
Add-ons
Install SSH & Web Terminal
